discussion_comments.comment_body: AI Review: The visible `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabled` settings can contain an existing explicit `on`, but this now forwards only `chat.agent.sandbox.*`, whose enablement defaults to `off`; the legacy settings remain registered but are no longer consumed. Users with only the previous SDK opt-in therefore become unsandboxed after upgrade. Migrate explicit legacy values without overwriting explicit new values, or retain a compatibility fallback and deprecate the old settings.

AI Review: This unconditional skip also removes the schema-driven fallback on phone. The phone new-session `MobilePermissionPicker` renders permission levels and Learn More but does not consume the standalone sandbox toggle, while the other mobile picker exposes only Mode and Model, leaving no way to choose the new session sandbox state before creation. Add a sandbox row to the phone permission sheet, or skip this property only when a dedicated control is available.

Thank you for filing this PR, I think we need to find a better way,
I'll work with the Copilot CLI team to figure out whether there's a better way to pass this URI.
Updating environment variables could break other parts of the product as we have other extensions/code running in the same process that could be directly/indirectly using this same env variable.

@DonJayamanne 
I understand the arguments and share your concerns—manipulating and setting environment variables also feels a bit off to me.
On the flip side, we have to keep in mind that the entire agent app experience is currently blocked for GHE users. Parallel sessions with Copilot CLI and worktrees have basically been unusable for over four weeks now.
With that in mind, it might be worth merging a quick fix (like this PR) for now, while we work on a proper long-term solution via better CLI configuration in parallel.
Fixed. Added `delete process.env['COPILOT_API_URL']` to the `afterEach()` hook so the env var is cleaned up after each test and can't leak into subsequent suites.

Done in 3973ede — back to a single status-gated welcome entry, same shape as `main`.

You were right that the fork bought nothing: both blocks already invoked the same command and differed only in the label. Collapsing them left `CONTEXT_MARKETPLACE_AUTH_PROVIDER` with no consumers, so the context key is deleted too. The browser layer no longer references either provider id, and it also stopped importing `DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_SIGN_IN_COMMAND`.
